questions.stem: What is the term used for atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons?
questions.solution: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, which gives them different mass numbers. Isotones have the same number of neutrons but different protons, isobars have the same mass number but different protons, and isomers are different arrangements of atoms within a molecule.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements has an electronic configuration of 2, 8, 1?
questions.solution: Sodium has an atomic number of 11, which means it has 11 electrons. These electrons fill the shells as 2 in the first, 8 in the second, and 1 in the third, resulting in the configuration 2, 8, 1. Oxygen has 8 electrons, giving it a configuration of 2, 6. Chlorine has 17 electrons, leading to 2, 8, 7. Argon has 18 electrons, resulting in 2, 8, 8. Therefore, sodium is the correct answer.

questions.stem: According to Rutherford's model of the atom, where are the electrons located?
choices: Surrounding the nucleus in fixed orbits
questions.solution: Rutherford's model describes the electrons as revolving around the nucleus, similar to how planets orbit the Sun. This model introduced the concept of a central nucleus with electrons moving in orbits around it. The other options are incorrect because they either place electrons inside the nucleus or suggest they are spread out in a way that contradicts the model.

questions.stem: In the gold foil experiment, most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without deflection. What does this observation suggest about the structure of an atom?
choices: The atom is mostly solid with no empty space
The atom has a dense, positively charged nucleus
The atom is mostly empty space with a small, dense nucleus
The atom has equal amounts of positive and negative charge
questions.solution: The observation that most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without deflection suggests that most of the atom is empty space. This supports the idea that the nucleus, which is dense and positively charged, occupies only a very small part of the atom. The other options are incorrect because they either contradict the experimental results or misinterpret the findings.

questions.stem: An atom has 79 protons and a mass number of 197. What will be the mass number if two neutrons are added to its nucleus?
questions.solution: The mass number of an atom is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons. In this case, the original mass number is 197, which means there are 197 - 79 = 118 neutrons. Adding two more neutrons gives 118 + 2 = 120 neutrons, making the new mass number 79 + 120 = 199. The option '198' is incorrect because it adds only one neutron. The option '200' is incorrect because it adds three neutrons. The option '197' is incorrect because it does not account for the added neutrons.

hi.stem: एक परमाणु में 79 प्रोटॉन हैं और द्रव्यमान संख्या 197 है। यदि इसके नाभिक में दो न्यूट्रॉन जोड़े जाएं तो द्रव्यमान संख्या क्या होगी?
hi.solution: किसी परमाणु की द्रव्यमान संख्या प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन की संख्या के योग के बराबर होती है। इस मामले में मूल द्रव्यमान संख्या 197 है, जिसका अर्थ है कि 197 - 79 = 118 न्यूट्रॉन हैं। दो अतिरिक्त न्यूट्रॉन जोड़ने से 118 + 2 = 120 न्यूट्रॉन हो जाते हैं, जिसके कारण नई द्रव्यमान संख्या 79 + 120 = 199 हो जाती है। विकल्प '198' गलत है क्योंकि इसमें केवल एक न्यूट्रॉन जोड़ा गया है। विकल्प '200' गलत है क्योंकि इसमें तीन न्यूट्रॉन जोड़े गए हैं। विकल्प '197' गलत है क्योंकि इसमें जोड़े गए न्यूट्रॉनों की गणना नहीं की गई है।

questions.stem: If an atom has 18 neutrons and an atomic number of 17, what is its mass number?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 35. The mass number is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons. Since the atomic number is 17, the number of protons is also 17. Adding the 18 neutrons gives 17 + 18 = 35. The other options are incorrect because they do not match this calculation.

hi.stem: यदि एक परमाणु में 18 न्यूट्रॉन हैं और परमाणु संख्या 17 है, तो इसकी द्रव्यमान संख्या क्या है?
hi.solution: सही उत्तर 35 है। द्रव्यमान संख्या प्रोटॉनों और न्यूट्रॉनों की संख्या के योग के बराबर होती है। चूंकि परमाणु संख्या 17 है, इसलिए प्रोटॉनों की संख्या भी 17 है। 18 न्यूट्रॉन जोड़ने से 17 + 18 = 35 प्राप्त होता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे इस गणना के साथ मेल नहीं खाते।

questions.stem: Why did Rutherford’s model fail to explain atomic stability, while Bohr’s model succeeded?
choices: Rutherford’s model did not account for the attraction between electrons and the nucleus, while Bohr’s model did.
Rutherford’s model allowed electrons to lose energy and fall into the nucleus, while Bohr’s model prevented this.
Rutherford’s model explained the stability of atoms, while Bohr’s model did not.
Rutherford’s model proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus, while Bohr’s model did not.
questions.solution: Rutherford’s model failed to explain atomic stability because it did not account for the fact that electrons would lose energy and eventually fall into the nucleus. Bohr’s model succeeded by proposing that electrons move in fixed energy levels without losing energy. The option 'Rutherford’s model did not account for the attraction between electrons and the nucleus, while Bohr’s model did' is incorrect because both models acknowledged the attraction. The option 'Rutherford’s model explained the stability of atoms, while Bohr’s model did not' is incorrect because Rutherford’s model did not explain stability. The option 'Rutherford’s model proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus, while Bohr’s model did not' is incorrect because both models proposed this.

questions.stem: In an atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons. If all the electrons are replaced with hypothetical particles that have the same charge as electrons but are 500 times heavier, what will be the impact on the atom’s chemical properties?
questions.solution: Chemical properties depend on the number and arrangement of electrons. Since the hypothetical particles have the same charge as electrons, the electron configuration remains the same, and so do the chemical properties. The first option is correct because the charge and number of particles are the same. The other options are incorrect because they assume the chemical properties will change, which they do not.
